daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The Corruption Eradication Commission (KPK) has named the rector and vice-rector of Unsoed as suspects in a major corruption case involving new student admissions. The KPK detained both officials after alleging extortion schemes in which parents paid massive sums to secure admission for their children. In one case, parents paid Rp 650 million to a vice-rector for medical school admission, yet their child was still not accepted.

  • The KPK has uncovered three clusters of corruption by the Unsoed rector in the new student admission process.
  • The head of academic affairs at Unsoed allegedly received Rp 1.12 billion to facilitate the admission of new students.
  • A DPR member explained the central government's rationale for planning to take over management of non-permanent civil servants (PPPK).
  • A DPR member highlighted that teachers' salaries have not increased despite rising education budgets.
  • At a pretrial hearing for Febrie, a former official testified that naming a suspect within one day is unusual practice.
  • The Attorney General's Office refuted Febrie's defense arguments one by one, including claims of trading in influence and duplicate suspect designation.
  • Former Minister Yaqut's legal team asked the judge to scrutinize the indictment in his hajj quota corruption case to avoid disparities in law enforcement.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia and China have agreed to accelerate finalization of the Code of Conduct for the South China Sea. The push for completion of this long-negotiated framework comes as both countries seek to strengthen regional maritime cooperation and stability. The agreement was reached during bilateral discussions between Indonesian and Chinese officials.

  • Russian President Putin has revealed plans to meet President Prabowo in Vladivostok.
  • The Foreign Ministry noted that a visit by MIKTA ambassadors to the TNI peacekeeping center demonstrates commitment to maintaining world peace.
  • MIKTA ambassadors paid respect to Indonesian peacekeepers' sacrifices during their visit to the peacekeeping training center.
  • The TNI has mobilized 14,167 soldiers to support firefighting operations in Kalimantan.
  • Indonesia's embassy in Dakar is pushing to strengthen partnerships between ASEAN and West Africa.

Other

Coordinating Minister Airlangga stated that Indonesia's gold bank ecosystem has successfully transformed idle precious metal assets into productive value for the economy. The minister emphasized that this initiative allows gold owners to leverage their holdings more effectively rather than leaving them dormant. The gold banking system represents a significant innovation in Indonesia's financial sector infrastructure.

  • Trade Minister announced that the IEU-CEPA agreement will offer Indonesia's highest tariff commitments, with 90.4 percent of tariff posts immediately reduced to zero when the agreement takes effect next year.
  • Bank Indonesia reported that QRIS has reached 65.77 million users and is accepted by 44.86 million merchants nationwide.
  • Indonesian shrimp exports face a 13.9 percent U.S. tariff, which the government noted is lower than the rate imposed on Vietnam.
  • West Sumatra police arrested an Indian national and seized 1.4 kg of gold from illegal mining operations.
  • The National Disaster Agency reported that the Flores earthquake has damaged 1,378 schools affecting 177,678 students, with 923 schools remaining temporarily closed.
